sections.heading: Sepolia Shadow Fork Results
sections.summary: Two shadow fork rounds were run; first surfaced Nethermind, Besu, ethrex, and Lighthouse issues, second round went smoothly.
sections.body:
- Two rounds of Sepolia shadow forks were run the prior week.
- First round found issues:
  - Nethermind's 2.0 release missed some late test additions; fixes were already in their 2.1 release, which shipped before the second shadow fork.
  - Besu had empty blocks caused by peering issues specific to the shadow fork environment.
  - ethrex had P2P peering difficulties unique to the shadow fork setup; confirmed these will not affect Sepolia or other networks.
  - Lighthouse had fork-boundary-related PTC issues and builder onboarding problems, which were investigated and resolved.
- Second round went smoothly: Nethermind performed well, builder onboarding succeeded, and deposits worked.

sections.heading: FOCIL Devnet 0 Outage
sections.summary: FOCIL devnet 0 went down after a misconfigured rollout with too few validators and no supernodes caused irreversible column loss.
sections.body:
- Barnabas accidentally killed focil-devnet-0 while rolling out a new image update and enabling QUIC on CL clients.
- Root cause: no supernodes were online and only 100 validators per host were configured (instead of 128), so reconstruction failed.
  - Nodes diverged onto different forks and some data columns were permanently lost.
- Lesson learned: future devnets must ensure enough supernodes are running on the network.
- Parithosh noted the 100-validator misconfiguration was also partly his fault.

sections.heading: Sepolia Upgrade Readiness (Glamsterdam)
sections.summary: Sepolia Glamsterdam fork is scheduled for 6 October 2026 at 13:53 UTC; all clients confirmed readiness or near-readiness.
sections.body:
- Fork is less than 24 hours away at time of call.
- **EL client readiness:**
  - Geth: has a release ready for Sepolia; a pending fix is planned but not yet out; old version still works for Sepolia.
  - Nethermind: ready on version 2.1; confirmed by Ben Adams.
  - Besu: validators on Sepolia all upgraded; confirmed ready by Daniel Lehrner.
  - ethrex: ready, in a similar position to Geth with a last-minute finding from Nico (Lodestar) being worked on; expected to be resolved before fork.
  - Reth and Erigon: no representatives present; to be synced via Discord/async.
- **CL client readiness:**
  - Prysm: releasing v7.2.1 patch for builder configuration bug fix and enabling partial data columns by default; includes 200M gas limit schedule.
    - Version number clarified on-call: v7.2.1 (not v7.2.2 as initially posted by Potuz in the validator channel).
  - Lighthouse: released v8.3.0-rc.0 for Sepolia; a bug found on shadow fork causes incorrect proposal preferences just before fork; fix is on Unstable but may not ship as a new release; worst case is local builds for the first epoch. Has 200M gas limit set.
  - Teku: v96.9.1 ready for Sepolia; 200M gas limit PR was merged but likely after the release cut, so not included in the release; can be specified via command line. A follow-up release is planned but won't land before Sepolia.
  - Nimbus: ready with release candidate 26.10.0.
  - Lodestar: ready with gas schedule set; Nico Flaig plans to run a builder on Sepolia and shared the URL.
  - Grandine: v3.0.0-rc.0 ready for Sepolia with 200M gas limit set; working on minor fixes.
- Ben Adams raised concern that many Nethermind nodes on Sepolia are running very old versions without the fork release; Parithosh suggested pushing updates via the validator chat but noted limited coordination options beyond that.

sections.heading: EIP Last Call Status for Glamsterdam Proposals
sections.summary: Pooja requested all Glamsterdam EIP authors move their proposals to Last Call status and submit PRs before the next EIP Editing Office Hour.
sections.body:
- Pooja Ranjan noted that ideally all Glamsterdam proposals should be in Last Call status now that testnet deployment is imminent.
- A [comment was added](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2242#issuecomment-5996049124) listing the needed PRs.
- Authors asked to submit PRs and add them as comments so they can be merged before the next ACD call.

sections.heading: Builder Onboarding on Sepolia
sections.summary: Builders will not be active at the Sepolia fork due to Bepolia token requirements; deposits can be made immediately post-fork with normal Sepolia ETH.
sections.body:
- Barnabas explained that the Bepolia token requirement for the special Sepolia deposit contract makes pre-fork builder deposits impractical.
- Builder deposits were tested successfully on the shadow fork.
- Post-fork, the builder deposit contract accepts normal Sepolia ETH; deposits can be made immediately.
  - The deposit contract was already deployed approximately two weeks ago.
  - Nico noted builder index 0 is already his.
- Builders wanting to test before mainnet are advised to use Hoodi instead of Sepolia.

sections.heading: Client Release Communication and Versioning Process
sections.summary: Spencer asked how version bumps close to fork day are communicated; Parithosh explained it varies by network, relying on validator chats, blogs, and Twitter.
sections.body:
- Spencer raised the question of how validators learn about last-minute version bumps, noting new releases are happening within a day of the fork.
- Barnabas pointed to the [blog post](https://blog.ethereum.org/2026/09/17/glamsterdam-testnet-announcement#client-releases) as the source of truth for client versions.
- Parithosh explained the communication channels differ by network:
  - Sepolia and Hoodi: updates posted on the validator chat; most validators are there.
  - Mainnet: no central coordination location; relies on client release channels, Twitter, and blog posts combined.
- No formal process change was proposed.

sections.heading: Execution Gas Limit for eth_call after EIP-8037
sections.summary: Geth's eth_call was incorrectly capped at the single-transaction gas limit post-EIP-8037; Gary confirmed a fix; behavior to be specified in the execution-APIs repo.
sections.body:
- Maria Silva presented the issue: after [EIP-8037](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8037-state-creation-gas-cost-increase/25694/47), Geth's `eth_call` enforced the same gas limit as a single on-chain transaction (~16M gas), breaking use cases that simulate high-gas view functions (e.g., SVG renderers, quoters, aggregators).
  - Before EIP-8037, `eth_call` did not have this single-transaction limit.
- Gary from Geth confirmed he already has a fix covering `eth_call`, `trace_call`, and `eth_simulate`.
- Marius suggested the correct place to specify this behavior is the execution-APIs repo, not the EIP itself.
  - Maria agreed and noted that once Geth merges the fix, it should be reflected in the execution-APIs spec.
  - Chase Wright confirmed execution-APIs tests have not yet been upgraded for Glamsterdam; they are waiting on 2-3 PRs from go-ethereum to merge so they can bump the reference and hivechain.
- Jochem raised whether `eth_call` needs separate state-gas and execution-gas parameters; Maria clarified that putting all gas into execution gas is sufficient since execution gas can be used for both state and execution, and this mirrors pre-EIP-8037 behavior.
- No objections from other clients; Maria will follow up on Eth Magicians and verify the fix is merged.
